page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation. Local disk storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring attached block storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 4 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-threaded compute performance. In stress-ng single-core tests, the ecs.c8ae.xlarge scored in the top 10 percent, complemented by strong Geekbench single-core and text processing results in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the middle 50 percent average tier. However, memory-intensive and multi-threaded scaling workloads exhibit limitations. Small-block memory bandwidth, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing fall into the bottom 25 percent benchmark bracket. Database operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving throughput also measured in the lower quartile.

The instance offers high per-core single-threaded compute capability at a 1:2 RAM ratio, delivering solid single-core CPU return per resource unit without paying for unnecessary memory overhead. However, the limited 8.0 GB RAM capacity and reduced throughput in memory-bound or highly parallel tasks represent key architectural tradeoffs. The ecs.c8ae.xlarge is best matched to single-threaded compute tasks, lightweight web utilities, background batch processing, text processing applications, and moderate microservice workloads that do not require high memory density or bundled ephemeral storage.
